gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-maitree: Loud, steady strokes up top, then a softer hand below. Aaargh has no hairline anywhere, while Maitree, a text serif, swells gently from thin to stem; that pen-like give is the pair's real draw.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-noto-serif-hk: Noto Serif HK has a generous gap where each curve ends and crossbars slightly thinner than its stems. And under Aaargh's uniform curves, paragraphs of it would read with a steady, editorial pace.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-noto-serif-jp: Thick-walled and blunt: Aaargh draws its o as a ring of constant wall, while the body curves soften. Give Noto Serif JP a little more size so that soft contrast shows.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-noto-serif-sc: Aaargh draws a line that never changes with direction, round or straight. But Noto Serif SC thickens slightly at its sides, and that mild bar variation is the quiet strength of the pair.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-petrona: Dignified body, commanding heading: Aaargh keeps its horizontals no thinner than its verticals. Petrona, a serif of modest contrast like lightly engraved brass, would read steadily across paragraphs without jolting.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-radley: Aaargh traces every letter like a technical drafting pen, one steady line from stem to bowl, no shading anywhere. Radley's lightly shaded texture is the gap that matters most here.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-roboto-serif: Big-eyed letters spaced well apart, with a faint charcoal-like pressure shadow, give the text a worn, human texture. Roboto Serif, a text serif, then sits under Aaargh, whose line width never shifts between curves and straights.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-sedan: Aaargh looks like glass tubing bent into letters, its line holding steady through every curve and every straight run. Sedan, a text serif, adds a mellow mid-range stroke contrast beside it.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-shippori-mincho: Marker-bold up top: Aaargh traces its letters in one thick line, with a generous way into every e. Shippori Mincho varies its stroke weights gently, and that quiet shift is the pair's best trait.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-stix-two-text: STIX Two Text pulls its terminals back from where each curve closes, and its thins run only slightly lighter than thicks. STIX Two Text moves moderately against Aaargh, whose strokes are as constant as bent wire.
